findings: Every dimension uses the same fill-in sentence template and repeats one supposed limitation without demonstrating distinct consequences under the six criteria. This does not establish compliance with the no-duplicate-deduction rule.

Several positive reasons are wrongly called limitations, e.g. pro-best-not-necessary says its principal evidential limitation is that the distinction is sufficiently warranted; pro-discrepancy-two-direction-effect says calibration is limited because the two evidential vectors are properly separated. These are not coherent evaluative rationales.

Every dimension requires a meaningful explanation of the actual source feature as it bears on that criterion, distinguishing inferential form, evidential warrant, engagement, burden contact, clarity, and calibration. No source defect may be copied into all six criteria without separate explained consequences.

Preserve distinct adopted burdens, conditional source premise, limited persecution inference, later qualified testimony threshold and every exclusion. No rating direction, peer output or totals supplied.
